case_name: Rajender Singh and Others v State Of Haryana
respondent:
State Of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

9 January 2009
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 1662-1663 OF 2005 WITH CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 355 OF 2006 WITH CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 615 OF 2008
The Judgment was delivered by : Lokeshwar Singh Panta, J.
1. Seven accused, namely, Suraj Bhan (A-1), Balraj (A-2), Ram Niwas (A-3), Rajender Singh (A-4), Dharambir (A-5), Sube Singh (A-6) and Sajjan Singh (A-7) were tried by Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Rohtak, in Sessions Case No. 119 of 2002 for committing the murder of Dinesh aged about 20 years.
2. statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code
Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: Seven accused were tried by Learned Additional Sessions Judge, Rohtak, in Sessions Case No. 119 of 2002 for committing the murder of Dinesh aged about 20 years.
The incident leading to the prosecution of the appellants occurred on 29.05.2002.

Dinesh, son of Dharambir (PW-1) complainant, had gone to Delhi for ascertaining the date of his interview for recruitment to the Police Force of Delhi Government, but till late night he did not return to his village Sundana, Tehsil Kalanaur, District Rohtak.

On coming to know the fact of confinement of his son by A-1, PW-1 alongwith his father Sube Singh (PW-11) and uncle Raghbir Singh rushed to the house of A-1, where they found the outer door of the house bolted from inside.
They all heard the shrieks of Dinesh 'maar diya, maar diya'.

Thereupon, they peeped through the window and saw that all the appellants including A-6 (since acquitted) had made Dinesh to lie down on the floor of the room, his hands and legs were tied with a rope.
In the electric bulb light and within their sight, A-1 inserted a 'danda' (wooden stick) in the anus of Dinesh, who cried loudly in pain.
On seeing the occurrence, PW-1, PW-11 and Raghbir Singh raised an alarm and forcibly broke open the door of the room.
On seeing them, the appellants fled away and took 'danda' and piece of rope with them.
They attended Dinesh, but he succumbed to his injuries at the spot.
issues: Whether the evidence produced in this case is sufficient and convincing to warrant the conviction of the appellants?
Whether the trial court erred in convicting A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, A-5 and A-7 under Section 302/342 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code?
petitioner_arguments: The evidence produced in this case is not sufficient and convincing to warrant the conviction of the appellants.
The evidence of PW-1 and PW-11 could not be accepted as they are both interested witnesses related to the deceased.
PW-1, PW-9 and PW-10 in their deposition have given a concocted version which casts severe doubts about truthfulness of the prosecution case.

The evidence appearing on record against the appellants is verbatim version which was taken into consideration by the trial court with regard to the acquittal of A-5, A-6 and A-7 and, therefore, the case of the appellants cannot be decided on any other scale and should have been treated at par for giving benefits of doubt to the appellants as it was considered for the acquittal of A-5, A-6 and A-7.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution has established its case beyond reasonable doubt.
The evidence of PW-1 and PW-11 is reliable and trustworthy.
The trial court did not err in convicting A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, A-5 and A-7 under Section 302/342 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
court_reasoning: The Court has carefully considered the evidence on record and finds that it is sufficient to establish the guilt of the appellants beyond reasonable doubt.
The Court notes that the trial court did not err in convicting A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, A-5 and A-7 under Section 302/342 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
holding: The appeals are dismissed. The conviction and sentence of A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, A-5 and A-7 are upheld.
